messages.subject: Negative learning rate for bandit2arm model
messages.subject_clean: Negative learning rate for bandit2arm model
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

My name is Simon, I'm a PhD student at CIMH in Mannheim, Germany, and I'm doing research on interactions of pain and reward.

I have an experiment in which a drug manipulation even seems to reverse operant learning in a simple 2 armed-bandit task (using pain relief as a reward).

Therefore, I tried to model a negative learning rate. To achieve this, I edited the stan file (bandit2arm_delta.stan) and set vector<lower=-1, upper=1>A. Following the update (#107 <https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/pull/107/commits/e30e6a712246ecc81d3c6e724b527070dcb0a87d>) made on the choiceRT_ddm model to facilitate a negative drift rate, I also changed A[i] = Phi_approx(mu_pr[1] + sigma[1] * A_pr[i]); to A[i] = mu_pr[1] + sigma[1] * A_pr[i];.
This model runs but it gives some strange results: the model plot shows me an estimated mu_A with a mean of around 0.5 while the single subjects' estimated A parameters are all in a range [-0.1, 0.1]. How can this be?
I have also set up a bandit2arm model with more parameters (comparable to the bandit4arm_4par model) and allowed the parameters R(reward sensitivity) and P (punishment sensitivity) to vary between negative and positive values. This model gives me a lot divergent transitions, even with a high number of iterations.
So I wonder if I misunderstood the way the models are set up in Stan..

Especially the first of these models seems to model the data quite well! Running a simulation with the obtained subjectwise parameters I can reproduce the number of correct choices (choice of the arm with a better net outcome) quite nicely...
Thus, I'd really like to get the models running and any ideas/input on this is highly appreciated!
Thanks a lot!

Best wishes,

Simon

P.S.: I also opened an issue at Github before I stumbled across this google group. I apologize if that was the wrong place to seek for support and I'm happy to close the issue if that was the case!

messages.subject_clean: Negative learning rate for bandit2arm model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

This sounds like an interesting application!

My first thought is that, you may have missed the part in the "generated quantities" block where you need to change:

"mu_A = Phi_approx(mu_pr[1])" to

"mu_A = mu_pr[1]"

in order to reflect the corresponding change you made in the transformed parameters block. Actually, given that you are seeing mu_A = .5 (which is what we would expect from the phi_approx transform if the actual mu_p[1] value was around 0), I am pretty sure that is the issue!

I think the issues you are encountering with the negative sensitivity parameters may be that, if the learning rate can also be negative, there is likely an identifiability issue between the sensitivity and learning rate parameters. If you plot person-level (or group-level) pairs plots, do they look highly co-linear? The models could still fit the data well even with this issue, despite the parameters not being recoverable. That would not necessarily explain the divergent transitions, though, but would be a good thing to check.

(and yes, I think it would be best to close the GitHub issue given that this is related to a modification of the original code)

Best,
Nate

I have an experiment in which a drug manipulation even seems to reverse operant learning in a simple 2 armed-bandit task (using pain relief as a reward).

Therefore, I tried to model a negative learning rate. To achieve this, I edited the stan file (bandit2arm_delta.stan) and set vector<lower=-1, upper=1>A. I have also set up a bandit2arm model with more parameters (comparable to the bandit4arm_4par model) and allowed the parameters R(reward sensitivity) and P (punishment sensitivity) to vary between negative and positive values. This model gives me a lot divergent transitions, even with a high number of iterations.
So I wonder if I misunderstood the way the models are set up in Stan..

Especially the first of these models seems to model the data quite well! Running a simulation with the obtained subjectwise parameters I can reproduce the number of correct choices (choice of the arm with a better net outcome) quite nicely...
Thus, I'd really like to get the models running and any ideas/input on this is highly appreciated!
Thanks a lot!

Best wishes,

Simon

P.S.: I also opened an issue at Github before I stumbled across this google group. I apologize if that was the wrong place to seek for support and I'm happy to close the issue if that was the case!

You were absolutely right, I missed to also change the respective line in the generated quantities block. This solved the issue of the group level parameter which now seems to reflect the single subject parameters for A. Great! Thanks!

For the model in which I allowed the sensitivity parameters to be negative I did deliberately not allow the learning rates (Arew and Apun) to be below zero as I expected that to cause issues.
Here is what the pairs plot on the group level parameters looks like:
I'd interpret that there is an issue with the separate learning rates that creates issues with the identifiability, correct?
Should I try to model a single learning rate instead?

Thank you!

Best wishes,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Great! Glad that was a simple fix.

And thanks for the plot. Could you include the "sigma" parameters (i.e. group-level SDs) in the pairs plot as well? I am wondering if there are any funnels showing up their, which could produce all these divergent transitions.

As for identifiability, I would say that these actually look good in terms of no extreme trade-offs. It is interesting that some of the samples for the learning rates are so far from the mass of the rest of the posterior, though. Including the SD might be able to help.

Could you also include your Stan code here?

Best,
Nate

messages.subject: DDM and delta parameter
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I have two questions about the choiceRT_ddm model:
1. Is there a reason that the delta parameter is not reparametrized (except for the non-centered reparametrization)? From my understanding, delta > 0, so I wonder why in your stan models (choiceRT_ddm) this paramater is not constrained?
2. In my task I have different levels of visual coherence (0.05, 0.1, 0.35, 0.5). Should it affect the delta parameter somehow or should I fit the wiener distribution with one fixed delta nevertheless?

Thank you! (And thanks for this great package.)

Daniel

Best,

messages.body_plain:
Dear Nate,

I managed to get rid of the divergent transitions by removing any constraints on the mu_P and mu_R parameters in the transformed parameters block.
Looking at the pairs plot does not really tell me why this prevents the divergent transitions.

However, if I keep parameter restrictions in both, the transformed parameter block (vector<lower=P_min, upper=P_max>[N] P;) and the generated quantities block (vector<lower=-30, upper=30>[N] mu_P;) I get a lot of exceptions and I cannot really run the model:
Chain 1: Exception: validate transformed params: mu_P is 32.2043, but must be less than or equal to 30  (in 'model2a522198448_bandit2arm_delta_5par_negsens' at line 113)

Nevertheless, I am now able to run the model and get reasonable parameter estimates. This does solve my initial issue.
I just wonder if this affects parameter estimation in some way, and if so, if I should worry about this... Any feedback is welcome!

Thanks!

Best wishes,
Simon

messages.subject: Setting up repeated measures model
messages.body_plain:
Dear hBayesDM users,

I am trying to extend the bandit2arm_delta  model for a repeated measures experiment.
Basically, I have 3 drug conditions, Placebo and 2 different neuromodulators.
My aim is to estimate different parameters for each subject in each of the conditions (plus mean parameter), and also to compare such a model to a model that models the same parameter for each subject in each of the drug conditions (and the same mean parameter for all conditions).

Thus, in a first approach I tried to model the Placebo condition (condition 1) the same way as in the original model, i.e. each parameter (A and tau) as A_c1 = mu_pr_c1 + sigma_c1 * A_pr_c1  (where c1 is condition 1). Then for the other conditions I added an additional mu, sigma, and subject parameter: A_c2 = mu_pr_c1 + sigma_c1 * A_pr_c1 + mu_pr_c2 + sigma_c2 * A_pr_c2 .
I would expect this to result in mu_pr_c2 reflecting the difference of my parameter (e.g. A) from the Placebo condition.

In a second approach I tried to model mu_pr  for each condition separately, i.e. A_c1 = mu_pr_c1 + sigma_c1 * A_pr_c1, A_c2 = mu_pr_c2 + sigma_c2 * A_pr_c2, etc.
I would expect this to model parameters as if I did this in separate models but to offer the opportunity to compare this to a model with a single parameter for all conditions.

However, both trials resulted in a huge number of divergent transitions, bad R-hat, low ESS, etc., even though I used max_treedepth = 20 and adapt_delta = 0.999.
So I wonder if something is wrong with my model specification. Also , I don't have a lot experience with Bayesian statistics in general and Stan in particular.

I attached the Stan files with my approaches described above.
Any feedback, suggestion, or help would be highly appreciated!

Thanks in advance!

Best wishes,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: DDM and delta parameter
messages.body_plain:
Hi Daniel,

Thanks for using it!

re (1), I think we originally had it so that delta>0, but then another user requested a change since there are certain task designs wherein a delta<0 may make sense.

re (2), this would depend on the theory you are aiming to test, I assume. Unfortunately, the current structure does not allow for estimating different deltas within conditions for the DDM, although the LBA model is currently equipped to do so. That said, I would check out the LBA model if you are interested in condition effects, or alternatively something like HDDM (http://ski.clps.brown.edu/hddm_docs/) if you would like to stick with the DDM.

Best,
Nate

I have two questions about the choiceRT_ddm model:
1. Is there a reason that the delta parameter is not reparametrized (except for the non-centered reparametrization)? From my understanding, delta > 0, so I wonder why in your stan models (choiceRT_ddm) this paramater is not constrained?
2. In my task I have different levels of visual coherence (0.05, 0.1, 0.35, 0.5). Should it affect the delta parameter somehow or should I fit the wiener distribution with one fixed delta nevertheless?

Thank you! (And thanks for this great package.)

Daniel
